responsibility: This module is GCC's C++ front end: it parses C++ source, builds and manages the C++-specific AST and declaration/type structures, enforces language rules, and lowers accepted programs into the generic/GIMPLE forms used by the middle end. Its major file families cover parsing and lexer integration (parser, lex), name binding and declarations (name-lookup, decl, decl2, friend), core semantic analysis and type checking (semantics, typeck, typeck2, cvt, call, expr), class/template machinery and ABI-sensitive C++ object model support (class, search, method, init, pt, mangle, rtti, except), constant evaluation and newer language features (constexpr, constraint, logic, lambda, coroutines, contracts, modules), diagnostics and developer inspection support (error, cxx-pretty-print, dump, ptree), and the front-end-to-middle-end bridge plus C++-specific instrumentation or emission decisions (cp-gimplify, cp-ubsan, optimize, repo, vtable-class-hierarchy, g++spec, lang hooks). For localization, parser-related files explain token/grammar and recovery problems, call/typeck files separate overload and conversion ranking from general expression well-formedness, pt files own template substitution and instantiation state, and constexpr files own constant-evaluation execution and diagnostics. Together these files implement C++ parsing, semantic validation, template instantiation, object model layout, ABI naming/emission, and feature lowering in a way that distinguishes gcc/cp from other language front ends and from target-specific back-end code.
